overview: Grenada is a small island country in the south-eastern Caribbean, made up of the island of Grenada and smaller islands including Carriacou and Petite Martinique. Its capital is St. George's. Grenada became independent from the United Kingdom in 1974. It is known as the 'Isle of Spice' because it grows so much nutmeg, which even appears on its flag.

geography.text: Grenada is a volcanic island with mountains and rainforest in the centre, crater lakes, and beaches around its coast, such as Grand Anse. Its smaller islands to the north are part of the Grenadines chain, which it shares with Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

history.text: Grenada's Kalinago people resisted European settlers until the French took the island in the 1650s; it passed to Britain in 1763. Grenada became independent in 1974. In 1979 a revolution brought Maurice Bishop to power, and after he was killed in 1983, the United States invaded.

events.title: French conquest
events.text: The French take Grenada from the Kalinago.

events.title: US invasion
events.text: US troops invade after the killing of Maurice Bishop.

events.title: Hurricane Ivan
events.text: The hurricane damages most homes on the island.

government.text: Grenada is a constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth, with the British monarch as head of state, represented by a Governor-General. The Prime Minister leads the government. The country includes the islands of Carriacou and Petite Martinique.

economy.text: Grenada is called the 'Spice Isle' because it grows nutmeg, mace, cinnamon and cocoa. It is one of the world's largest nutmeg exporters. Tourism and a large medical university also support the economy.

culture.text: A nutmeg appears on Grenada's flag. The island's Spicemas carnival is held every August. An underwater sculpture park off its coast was one of the first of its kind in the world.

items.title: Underwater Sculpture Park
items.text: Statues placed on the seabed since 2006 to form a reef.

sport.text: Athletics brings Grenada its biggest successes. Kirani James won Olympic gold in the 400 m in 2012, Grenada's first Olympic medal, and the country won more Olympic medals per person than almost anyone in 2024. Cricket is also very popular.
